lines.text: Welcome to Dota 2 Drafting Tool and thank you so much for downloading this application!
This tutorial is to help you find the ropes to get the maximum benefit out of this tool.
You can see below control buttons for going ahead a step, skipping a step, and for exiting the tutorial.
So if you feel like just finding the ropes yourself that's fine too. But, 'Don't say I never gave you anything.'
You see that giant hero grid over there? Yeah, that is YOUR hero grid.
You go ahead and click a hero with your left mouse button and a hero gets picked to the team indicated up here.
Now... Ugh, go away you.
Hmm... which one should we do... How about... Dazzle! Go ahead, click Dazzle with your left mouse button and see what happens!
Oh gosh... I got ahead of myself again. There's over 120 heroes here, how on earth do you expect to find a hero from all of these options?

lines.hint: Type Dazzle, then left-click his portrait.
lines.text: But hey, I got just the thing for you. Go ahead and type out the name "dazzle" and see what happens.
He-Hey! That's the one! Good job! You're a natural.
Now, as you can see, a bunch of heroes are already raring to go into battle with good old Dazzle here.
The higher the number, the better that hero fits your current draft. This is your equivalent of a Town Portal Scroll. You use this information to the best of your ability and good things will follow.
For future reference this is not a legally binding promise and this tool does not take any responsibility for the actual match outcomes.
Right. Now that we've gotten ourselves the best of the best supports selected, how about we choose some heroes to the enemy team as well.
As you previously saw, this label here is actually a 'change picking side' button that you can use to change the team you are picking for.

lines.hint: Change the picking side and choose Weaver.
lines.text: Now, let's say your opponents go ahead and pick Weaver position 4 as a response to your Dazzle. Go on, change the picking side and click on Weaver.
Nicely done! As you can see here some heroes thought twice once the Weaver showed his face.
It would seem that wolves indeed do need armor, contrary to what Lycan claims.
'The user can also press F2 to switch picking side quickly'? What does this even mean?
Who wrote this in here. Must've been the summer intern when I wasn't looking...
I did a little research into all these F-controls and apparently it is also possible to select heroes for either team whenever you want.
Apparently grabbing hold of a hero's hand, and walking them to their appropriate team works regardless of pick selection side.

lines.hint: Drag and drop Axe to the enemy team and Slark to the ally team.
lines.text: This one is something I've never heard of, but go on. Try and walk Axe to the enemy team and walk Slark to the ally team.
Oh. It actually worked. I... hadn't thought of that.
So... Look here! You can see heroes within the recommendations that have purple numbers below their scores.
The purpose of these purple numbers is to highlight a key aspect of your team composition that is currently missing.
Initiators recieve a bonus after 2 picks, pushers and disablers after 3 picks.
Do what you will with this information, I'm not your dad.
It seems our Dazzle is about to have a terrible time. Perhaps a wise player would ban the Axe either right after picking Dazzle or beforehand.
Good thing you can reverse a pick by clicking on the hero's portrait in the draft panel.

lines.hint: Click Axe's portrait in the enemy team to remove him.
lines.text: Go ahead, remove Axe from the enemy team.
Now, when looking into Axe's soul it seems he is a bit anxious being back with all these beefy boys.
So, how about we give Axe his own little home within the ban list?
You can right click on any hero currently not picked or banned to ban them.
Apparently the same removal functionality works to banned heroes too.

lines.hint: Find Axe in the hero grid and right-click his portrait.
lines.text: So yeah, go on and ban that Axe!
There we go! Although, now axe is looking extra sad with his little greyscale filter on his image. Poor thing.
Now that Axe has been put in the doghouse, it's time we start inspecting the recommendation feed.
Every ally and enemy is taken into consideration. Picked and banned heroes won't be recommended. Simple enough.

lines.hint: Hover over Batrider in the recommendation feed.
lines.text: What? That isn't enough? Fine. Hover over our good friend Batrider in the recommendation feed, and let's see where that number comes from.
As you can see, Batrider seems to be loved by Dazzle, disliked by Slark, and particularly unwelcome in Weaver's company.
Why? Don't ask me. I don't get paid enough for this.
The +6.76 beside Dazzle is a strong positive contribution to Batrider's score. Apparently these two get along rather well.
The +4.15 against Weaver is another positive contribution: this matchup favours Batrider. As it turns out, fire is the best pesticide.
Slark contributes -1.07. Add the +2 initiation bonus we discussed, and the total comes to 11.84. There. I've done the maths. Nobody make a habit of asking.
Now, you might be thinking, "Slark is already our carry. I don't need Faceless Void or Drow Ranger fighting him for the last hits."
And you'd be right.
Worry not. I've placed some special buttons down here just for you. They filter the recommendations by hero type, including heroes tagged as supports.

lines.hint: Enable Support, switch to Ally Team, then find Omniknight in the hero grid and left-click him.
lines.text: Change the recommendation feed to Support-only and pick Omniknight for the ally team. You can find him in the hero grid using the search we practised.
I genuinely hope the Omniscience can guide these clowns to victory...

heroPool.title: Your hero pool

reactions.supports: Well, if it isn't the friendly neighbourhood support who claims their MMR is being dragged down by their core players.
reactions.carries: Look out, people! Main character syndrome is contagious!
reactions.techies: Don't lie to any of us. You wish you were playing Old Techies.
reactions.microOne: How many games did you have to lose before you mastered that abomination?
reactions.microBoth: How many games did you have to lose before you mastered those abominations?

heroPool.firstUnavailableText: {firstHero} is already picked or banned, so they won't be recommended. Let's judge {firstAvailable} instead. Your three strongest available pool heroes appear here.
heroPool.unavailableText: Every hero you chose is already picked or banned. You've somehow managed to outdraft your own hero pool. The pool suggestions are empty, but we can still open the full breakdown.

lines.text: Now we can really get this party started. Remove that Support filter from the recommendations first.
Okay. Now check these controls over here: Edit Pool, Clear Bans and Clear All.
These are Buttons For The Convenience Of Indolent Representatives Of The Human Race. B.F.T.C.O.I.R.O.T.H.R. for short. Rolls right off the tongue.
We'll just call them universal draft controls. Two of the buttons are self-explanatory.
But this third one here contains one of the most useful ways to personalise this tool.
Edit Pool switches the hero grid into pool editing mode. Click a hero to add them to your pool. Click them again to remove them. A rare case of the buttons doing exactly what they look like they do.
In normal use, I'll remember your pool between launches. These tutorial choices are just a rehearsal, so your saved pool stays untouched.

lines.hint: Enable Edit Pool and choose any five heroes. Click again to remove a selection.
lines.text: Let's test this thing. Toggle pool editing on and select any five heroes to represent you as a player. Choose wisely. Or don't. I'll be judging either way.
Five heroes. Five opportunities to blame the draft. Excellent.
Hmm... Interesting... So you chose {poolNames}.
Very unorthodox choices. Do you pride yourself on your uniqueness? This definitely isn't the thousandth time I've seen this collection. No, no.

lines.hint: Click EDITING to finish editing your hero pool.
lines.text: Where was I? Right. Finish editing your hero pool.

lines.hint: Turn on the Hero Pool filter.
lines.text: Now enable hero pool filtering in the recommendation feed. Let's see which of your favourites has the least terrible prospects.
Now we can judge just how badly your game as {firstHero} might go with these allies and enemies. Your three strongest available pool heroes appear up here.
What? Not every hero is visible? Of course they aren't. We have to keep this feed useful. I can't just bloat the whole thing with a personal indictment of every hero you play.

lines.hint: Open the full hero pool breakdown using its info button.
lines.text: If you insist on the full indictment, this handy button here opens the complete breakdown. Go on. You asked for it.

These scores keep updating as you pick and ban heroes. Picked and banned heroes are excluded even here. A recommendation for a hero you can't pick would be a rather impressive waste of everyone's time.

lines.hint: Close the full hero pool breakdown.
lines.text: You can close this window now, and we'll continue this definitely not bloated and overexplained tour.
There. A personalised hero pool. That should narrow down the list of things you can blame me for.

sideSwitchEasterEgg.text: Yes, the button works. Thank you for your independent quality assurance.
sideSwitchEasterEgg.escapeText: Oh. That's new. You've annoyed the button so much it's developed a survival instinct. I'm beginning to understand how it feels. Finish the task. I'll see if I can talk it down.
sideSwitchEasterEgg.runawayHint: The button has escaped. Use F2 to switch sides and complete the task to bring it back.

interruptions.text: Dazzle has specifically told me for the purposes of this tutorial not to be allied with any hairy men.
Slark would so obviously eat this Weaver. That won't do.
What did I just say about not picking Dazzle into Axe?!
Hey! If you are that impatient you might as well just quit the whole thing.
Hold on there pal, a toddler must walk before they can run.
An excellent demonstration of what I wasn't asking you to do.
Who gave you free will? Was it that damn intern again?!
There should be some helpful explanation here somewhere... Oh wait. That's me.
That was very nearly a completely different instruction.
